tasks_completed.description: Refactored ToolFullView.tsx to always render generic sections (Description, Input, Output/Error) alongside specialized views
tasks_completed.changes: Changed from either/or rendering (specialized XOR generic) to always showing Description + Input + Specialized + Output/Error. Extracted 6 helper components (ToolDescriptionSection, ToolInputSection, ToolOutputSection, ToolErrorSection, ToolEmptyOutputSection, ToolRawJsonSection) to comply with function line-count limits.
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause was the ternary branch at line 30 that rendered ONLY SpecializedFullView when registered, completely skipping generic Description/Input/Output sections. Edit and Agent tools had specialized views, so users never saw their parameters or output.

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: N/A - original design decision, not a regression
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: ToolFullView was designed with either/or logic: specialized views completely replaced generic sections. This made sense initially but became a UX gap as Edit and Agent tools only showed their specialized content without Description/Input/Output context.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Changed rendering from ternary (specialized XOR generic) to sequential (Description + Input + Specialized + Output/Error), so all tools show structured metadata regardless of whether they have a specialized view.

dev.qa_notes: Verify via Playwright on dev.life-ai.app: 1) Open an Edit tool detail page - should now show Description, Input Parameters, the diff view, and Output sections. 2) Open an Agent tool detail page - should show Description, Input Parameters, sub-tool list, and Output. 3) Open a Read tool (no specialized view) - should show Description, Input Parameters, Output as before. 4) Verify 'No Output' empty state only shows for non-specialized tools. 5) Check both desktop and mobile viewports. Pre-existing typecheck errors (SessionActionsNativeMenu.android.tsx, SidebarNavigator.tsx) are unrelated.
